subject: Civil Engineering
title: Sustainability in Construction
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sustainability in Construction usable.

hook.text: Construction consumes 40% of raw materials globally and generates 30% of solid waste.

buildup.text: LEED and BREEAM certify sustainable buildings — rating energy, water, materials, and indoor quality.

discovery.text: Recycled steel, low-carbon concrete, and reclaimed wood reduce embodied carbon significantly.

twist.text: Mass timber buildings store carbon — wood locks away CO₂ that the tree absorbed while growing.

climax.text: Net-zero buildings generate as much energy as they consume — possible with current technology.

punchline.text: Construction shapes the planet. Sustainable building is now essential.

quiz.question: How do mass timber buildings contribute to carbon reduction?
options: They are lighter, requiring fewer trucks to deliver materials to the site
Wood stores the carbon the tree absorbed while growing, locking CO₂ into the building
Timber buildings are always smaller, using less energy overall

details.summary: Sustainable construction minimizes environmental impact through energy-efficient design, recycled and low-carbon materials, waste reduction, water conservation, and green building certifications like LEED.
details.whyItMatters: Buildings and construction account for 39% of global energy-related carbon emissions. The industry must transform its practices to meet climate targets and regulatory requirements.
takeaways: Construction and demolition waste represents 30 to 40% of total solid waste
LEED and similar systems provide frameworks for measurable green building delivery
Life-cycle assessment evaluates total environmental impact from cradle to grave

faq.question: What is LEED certification and how is it achieved?
faq.answer: LEED, Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design, is a point-based green building rating system. Projects earn points in categories like energy performance, water efficiency, materials selection, indoor air quality, and site sustainability.

faq.question: How can construction waste be reduced on job sites?
faq.answer: Plan material orders to minimize offcuts. Require suppliers to take back packaging. Provide separate bins for wood, metal, concrete, and cardboard for recycling. Crush concrete and masonry on site for reuse as fill. Prefabricate components in factory-controlled settings where offcuts are minimized.
